title: Odd sampling behavior after weight-apply: oncall notes and corrective actions
content:
Summary:

This is a concise on-call writeup from the November 4 canary rollout where new weight artifacts were applied to the xlarge-v2 family in eu-west-1. Immediately after a staggered weight-apply, we observed a clear change in generation behavior: outputs were consistently longer or higher-entropy for a subset of traffic, and certain prompts produced repetitive or slightly semantically off completions. User-facing error rates were low (no 5xx spikes), but qualitative regression was obvious on the evaluation harness. We rolled back the deployment within 18 minutes.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture timeline and hypotheses from oncall.
- Record quick detection signals and mitigation steps for runbook inclusion.
- Assign follow-ups to fix root cause and prevent recurrence.

High-level impact:
- Business: minimal immediate customer impact because we detected in canary and rolled back before full rollout; one internal customer reported unusual completions for automated summarization tests.
- Scope: approx 3 canary pods (out of 80 in eu-west-1 canary ring) serving ~0.6% of production traffic were affected before rollback.
- Duration: ~18 minutes between first alert and full rollback.

Detection timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-04 09:03:12: Synthetic eval job 'smoke-gen-suite' (scheduled) started. It contains ~120 prompts representing short chat, summarization, SQL generation, and code.
- 09:03:26: Eval job flagged 17/120 prompts failing a heuristics check (unexpected token entropy > threshold or repetition score > 0.8).
- 09:03:30: Canary alert generated: 'generation-entropy-drift' fired (p95 entropy up by +23% relative to baseline). Pager notified sre-oncall.
- 09:04–09:07: Oncall triage (Priya, Maya). Checked pod logs, pprof traces, model manifests. No 5xx, no OOMs. Latency unaffected.
- 09:09: Evidence of inconsistent sampling RNG state seen in streaming logs for affected pods: seed initialization timestamp missing in bootstrap logs for one pod class.
- 09:12: Confirmed new weight artifacts (build 1789) had been applied to three canary worker groups at 09:01 through staggered weight-swap orchestration.
- 09:15: Decision to rollback canaries to previous weight manifest (build 1776).
- 09:21: Canary pods replaced; synthetic evals returned to baseline within 2 eval intervals. Rolling forward was halted.

Initial observations and quick hypotheses:
1) RNG/Seeding/context-state mismatch: affected pods exhibited missing seed reinitialization logs, which correlated with higher entropy outputs. Hypothesis: new runtime changed where RNG is seeded during weight apply, causing divergence across worker processes (some seeded, some not).
2) Quantization scale misapply: inspection of quant metadata showed an extra normalization multiplier (0.998) embedded in build 1789's quant header for one layer due to an upstream rounding patch in the quantizer. Slight logit scaling differences can noticeably change sampling distributions, especially for nucleus sampling thresholds.
3) Hybrid effect: both (1) and (2) may be compounding — slight per-token logit scale change + inconsistent RNG seeding = randomized behavior that deviates from expected generation patterns.

Why we rolled back quickly:
- Customer-visible quality regression on internal evals, and risk of wider user confusion.
- No errors requiring further debugging in prod (steady-state), so rollback minimized blast radius and preserved traces for investigation.

Immediate actions performed during incident:
- Disabled active rollout gate for build 1789 across all rings (hosted + dedicated).
- Reverted canary manifest to build 1776 via orchestration API: /api/v1/deployments/manifest/rollback --id=eu-west-1-canary --to=1776. (Command run by James)
- Re-ran synthetic evals and smoke tests until metrics stable for 2 consecutive intervals.
- Captured memory and CPU profiles for an affected pod and a healthy pod for offline diff. Saved artifacts to s3://redwood-incident-archives/2025-11-04/odd-sampling/
- Opened JIRA-INC-4321 and linked the rollback PR and logs.

Repro instructions (for engineers investigating):
1) Pull the failing build artifacts locally: gh pr checkout 1789; ./scripts/download-weights --manifest=1789 --region=eu-west-1 --subset=layer-19,layer-20
2) Start a local runtime with identical flags used in deploy: ./bin/runtime --serve-mode=canary --rng-policy=auto --quant-apply=meta-first
3) Run the synthetic suite: python infra/evals/run_suite.py --suite=smoke-gen-suite --endpoint=localhost:8080 --repeat=3 --log-level=debug 2>&1 | tee repro.log
4) Compare logits scale summary: python scripts/compare_logits.py --input=repro.log --baseline=s3://model-baselines/1776/logits_summary.json
5) Check RNG init log lines: grep -E "RNG init|seed set" logs/*. If missing, repro of issue likely reproducible.

Root cause (investigation so far):
- Preliminary root cause is a combination of two changes introduced close to each other in build 1789: (A) a change in the quantizer that added a per-layer normalization multiplier (rounding patch) and (B) a refactor in the serving runtime that moved RNG seed initialization after the weight-apply hook for a specific worker class.
- The quant rounding multiplier alone would have produced a tiny shift in logits (order of 0.2% magnitude), generally acceptable. However, because some processes ended up with RNG seeded and others not (seed timing inconsistency), sampling variance amplified the perceptual effect and pushed nucleus/top-p sampling behaviors across thresholds.
- In short: deterministic-seed expectation + tiny logit shift = visible sampling regression.

Logs & artifacts to check (S3 paths):
- s3://redwood-incident-archives/2025-11-04/odd-sampling/affected-pod-logs.tgz
- s3://redwood-incident-archives/2025-11-04/odd-sampling/profiles/*
- s3://model-manifests/build-1789/quant-metadata.json (contains per-layer multiplier, check layer 19)
- github:runtime PR 1789 (runtime refactor) and quantizer PR 318 (in quant package)

Post-incident mitigations (short-term):
- Blocked build 1789 from any non-consented rollouts. Build flagged in release system with "hold: sampling-regression" tag.
- Added an immediate check to the canary gating job that compares per-prompt top1/top5 probabilities and RNG initialization log presence. If missing, fail gate. (Quick patch rolled by Maya: infra/pipelines/gates/canary_gate.py#L200)
- Added a repro checklist to the incident JIRA and attached the commands above.

Longer-term action items (owners + rough ETA):
1) Ensure RNG seed initialization is deterministic and happens before any weight-apply hooks for all runtime worker classes. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (James). ETA: 2025-11-18.
2) Revert or adjust the quant rounding patch to avoid implicit scaling multipliers; add unit tests that assert quant metadata parity between reference quantizer and release artifacts. Owner: applied-ml/quant-team (Maya). ETA: 2025-11-20.
3) Add end-to-end parity checks for logit distributions as part of pre-rollout suite (compare per-token logits summary for 100 core prompts). Owner: eng-sre (Priya). ETA: 2025-12-02.
4) Update rollout runbook: include a check for RNG init logs and an explicit "parity entropy" threshold in canary gate. Owner: site-reliability-engineering. ETA: 2025-11-12 (runbook draft update)
5) Create a lightweight canary-only instrumentation metric: "generation.rng_seed_present" (bool) emitted during worker bootstrap. Owner: observability team. ETA: 2025-11-14.

Runbook additions (draft bullets to be added):
- If generation-entropy-drift fires during a rollout, immediately:
  1) Pause rollout and freeze manifest.
  2) Run synthetic eval suite and check for entropy drift > +15% p95.
  3) Check for RNG init logs on all new pods: kubectl logs -n serving <pod> | grep -E "RNG init|seed set".
  4) Compare per-prompt logits summary (lastest vs baseline). If any per-token mean shift > 0.5%, escalate to serving-runtime + applied-ml.
  5) If heuristics show semantic regression and no runtime error, rollback to last good manifest.

Lessons learned:
- Small numeric changes (quant metadata rounding) can have outsized qualitative impact when combined with timing nondeterminism.
- Our rollout gates emphasize latency and error metrics but not probabilistic output parity; we need a small suite of lightweight statistical checks to catch these regressions earlier.
- An explicit instrumentation point (RNG seed presence) would have allowed earlier detection without manual log greps.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How many other builds contain similar quant rounding changes? We need a scan of recent model builds to enumerate differences.
- Are there any downstream caches (prefix/KV) that could have cached outputs from affected canaries and served them later to clients? (Initial check: no prefix caches appear to have been populated for 1789.)

Contacts and channels used during incident:
- Slack: #sre-oncall (primary), #runtime-eng (cc), #applied-ml (cc)
- Pager: SRE oncall rotation (Priya)
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-4321

Postmortem plan and timeline:
- This document will be updated into a full postmortem if follow-ups uncover additional systemic issues. Preliminary postmortem due: 2025-11-20. Final postmortem (with root cause verified and tests added) due: 2025-12-10.

Appendix: quick diffs and helpful commands
- Compare quant metadata: jq '.layers[19].scale' s3://model-manifests/build-1789/quant-metadata.json && jq '.layers[19].scale' s3://model-manifests/build-1776/quant-metadata.json
- Check RNG lines across pods: kubectl get pods -l rollout=1789 -n serving -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl logs {} -n serving | grep -E "RNG init|seed set" | wc -l
- Re-run smoke eval locally against build 1789: ./scripts/deploy-local --manifest=1789 && python infra/evals/run_suite.py --suite=smoke-gen-suite --endpoint=localhost:8080

If you're investigating next: start with the quant metadata diff and the RNG init logs. Reach out to Maya for quantizer internals and James for runtime seed placement rationale.

— End of notes by Priya Kapoor
